title: Verification Standard — Valuing the Measured Savings of a True-Up Period, Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscriptions
content:
# Valuing the Measured Savings of a True-Up Period

Standard applied when the measured savings of a closing period are verified on a subscription under Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscriptions.

## The figures

**The verified savings** are the saved electricity valued at the unit cost, taken at the weather normalisation share, then at the attributed share, then at the coverage share, and rounded to the nearest cent once at the end; each share acts on the result of the step before it, and none of them acts on the baseline itself.

**The savings guaranteed for the period** are the tier's guaranteed share of the baseline standing on the subscription, valued at the same unit cost and rounded to the nearest cent.

## The quantities

1. **The saved electricity** is a quarter of the baseline standing on the subscription less the electricity the period's readings recorded over the three months ending on the day of the verification, that difference taken four times, and never less than nothing.
2. **The unit cost** is the average unit cost of the billed readings of the twenty-four months ending on that day — their cost totalled and divided by their electricity totalled.
3. **The weather normalisation share.** No weather normalisation share is taken off the measured saving; the whole of it stands, at 100 percent.
4. **The attributed share** is the whole of the measured saving, 100 percent.
5. **The coverage share** is the partial coverage share, 85 percent.

## Order of the arithmetic

The saved electricity is settled first, in kilowatt hours, and held at nothing where the period's use was no lower than its share of the baseline. It is then multiplied by the unit cost, and the three shares act one after another on the money figure — the valued saving at the normalisation share, that product at the attributed share, that product at the coverage share. Nothing is rounded until the last share has acted; the figure then reached is rounded to the nearest cent. The savings guaranteed are worked out separately from the baseline itself, the guaranteed share of it valued at the same unit cost and rounded to the nearest cent, and the shares never touch that figure.

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

A subscription carries a baseline of 1 200 000 kilowatt hours a year at a tier guaranteeing 8 percent. The billed readings of the last three months record 260 000 kilowatt hours; those of the last twenty-four months record 2 400 000 kilowatt hours at a cost of USD 288 000.00.

- Unit cost: 288000.00 divided by 2400000, that is USD 0.12 a kilowatt hour.
- Saved electricity: a quarter of 1200000 is 300000; less 260000 leaves 40000; taken four times, 160 000 kilowatt hours.
- Valued: 160000 multiplied by USD 0.12, that is USD 19200.00.
- At 100 percent, then 100 percent, then 85 percent: USD 16320.00 — the **verified savings**.
- Savings guaranteed: 8 percent of 1200000 is 96000 kilowatt hours, valued at USD 0.12, that is USD 11520.00.
